newsitem.title: JAPAN: Showa Denko cuts ethylene output at Oita complex.
newsitem.headline: Showa Denko cuts ethylene output at Oita complex.

text.p: Showa Denko KK said on Thursday that it had reduced production of ethylene at its Oita complex in western Japan from April, operating at 90 percent of the 730,000-tonne-a-year capacity.
The ethylene plant, consisting of two naphtha crackers, will continue to be operated at 90 percent of capacity until September, when regular maintenance is scheduled, the company said in a statement.
The cut was decided to reduce consumption of naphtha, it said.
Japanese petrochemical companies are suffering from a sharp increase in naphtha prices since late last year.
Showa Denko does not produce ethylene at its other plants, a company spokesman said.

Late last year, Showa Denko reduced its ethylene production slightly to cut its naphtha consumption but naphtha prices in Asia remain extremely high, compared with North America and Europe, due to strong demand for naphtha in Asia, the company said.
"Under the circumstances, we have further reduced ethylene production with a view to making a more significant cut in naphtha consumption," the company said.
